newsitem.title: SPAIN: Spain electricity demand up 1.3 pct Jan-May yr/yr.
newsitem.headline: Spain electricity demand up 1.3 pct Jan-May yr/yr.

text.p: Spanish electricity demand rose 1.3 percent year-on-year in the five months to May, the chairman of electricity sector association Unesa said on Wednesday.
Inigo de Oriol added that the calendar-adjusted figure showed an increase of 2.1 percent over the same period in 1996, which was a leap year.

In the five months to May, total Spanish electricity output rose 3.1 percent, with fossil-fuelled production rising 68 percent. Hydro output fell 28.8 percent while nuclear output was down 8.7 percent year-on-year, Oriol said.
"It should be pointed out that the fall in hydroelectric production is fundamentally due to the fact that 1996 was an exceptional year for rainfall," he told reporters.
He added that rainfall in the first few months of the year had been lower than usual, but the effect of more recent heavy rain had yet to be evaluated.

Asked whether electricity firms would have difficulty in adjusting to new sector regulations, Oriol said: "It'll be more difficult in one sense...but we'll also be able to optimise our assets better."
A bill recently sent to parliament, drawn up in agreement with electricity companies, aims to gradually deregulate the sector by 1999.
